My dear [Mrs Curteis](/person/2034)
First I must tell you of what perhaps you have seen in the [Guardian](/periodical/75), my dear [Miss Dyson](/person/464)’s death. She had been growing feebler and feebler for the last two years and had for months been wholly confined to bed, and unable to read even a letter, though she was constantly read to for the last fortnight she was almost unconscious, and slept herself away. She leaves a great blank behind her!
I am afraid it is too late to protest against Helen’s babies, except by word of mouth as I have done, for I can’t bear them[^1] But I think they have had their day - and the bad imitation will do more to disgust with them than my protest. Armine does not by any means die so you need not be afraid for him.[^2] I have him now in the midst of a naughty fit, quite sufficient to save his life.
Thank you so much for your kind thoughts about the game

Yours sincerely

C M Yonge


[^1]: John Habberton Helen\'s Babies (1876), a best-selling work for young people. CMY may perhaps have considered that it treated religion irreverently.
[^2]: Armine is a character in CMY\'s [Magnum Bonum](/book/131) (1879), serialized in MP January 1877-December 1879..
